[2026-08-27T01:36:12.178Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5472b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":5475,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"body\":\"It will be a while before we get to this, but various parts of the architecture are already designed with this in mind.\\n\\nWe should support running Blazor in two modes, auto-selecting which one is best for the current user\\u0026#39;s browser:\\n\\n * **On the browser\\u0026#39;s main JS thread**, which is necessary for older browsers that don\\u0026#39;t support WebWorker. The .NET/JS interop can continue using shared memory if we find it\\u0026#39;s necessary to have good perf on those older browsers (and thread safety is not difficult because it\\u0026#39;s all synchronous).\\n * **In a web worker (background thread) on more up-to-date browsers**. The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. We\\u0026#39;ll have to be careful around things like event handling to ensure that the asynchrony can\\u0026#39;t result in inconsistency of behaviour versus the synchronous single-threaded model. For example, we will need to force all event delivery to be async as far as the JS side is concerned, even in the non-worker-thread case.\\n\\n*[1] Strictly speaking, we could also do it with shared memory on even newer browsers that support SharedArrayBuffer. But if we can get satisfactory perf without this, it would be better to serialize because it would mean fewer combinations of browser scenarios, and saves us having to deal with potentially complex thread-safety concerns on the .NET side.*\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5475\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-minor\",\"affected-very-few\",\"not-on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"pavelsavara\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 12 Planning\",\"comments\":14,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":22,\"+1\":21,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":1,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2018-02-19T17:05:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T12:05:29Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67768,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"state\":\"CLOSED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67768\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. (No-nos like passing lambdas as parameters)\\n- One Child Component for some reason is rerendered 10 times on changes.\\n- Some component maybe throws unintended events which caues rerenders.\\n- A costly operation (Rest call) is executed while wating for the task to complete multiple renders happen.\\n- A REST Call is made in OnParametersSet() or OnAfterRender() and by error this rest call is executed multiple times since unexpected Rerenders.\\n\\nWith one Component this can be debugged with console messages in OnParametersSet() or OnAfterRender, but in case of a complex render three with different components this gets quite compilcated to diagnose Performance Bottlenecks.\\n\\nAlso it is often difficult to see which changes cause rerenders in child components. \\nOr which await calls for for responses from Webservices also cause rerenders between initiating the call and completing the call.\\n\\n## Potential Solution:\\n\\nSome possiblily / Component / API, which allows globally to trace all OnSetParameters, Renders etc. with execution times, to see\\nif renders happen too frequent, how long it is executed and what caues the bottlenecks.\\n\\nat first maybe an API to hook into the render events of all components would be maybe already enough. Otherwise I would need make a custom ComponentBase class which traces all Steps like BuildRenderTree() or OnAfterRender().\\n\\n## Example\\n\\nA example output log\\n\\n```\\nNavigation.Component1 InitalizeAsync() took 100 Milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Inital Render:\\nNavigation.Component1 BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent Initalize() took 400 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Inital Render:\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because parameter change.\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because parameter change.\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because parameter change.\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because eventhanlder onclick\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\n```\\n\\nA integration into the Performance Monitor is maybe possible in Blazor Server Side but on the Blazor Webassembly side\\nonly general Browser tools for Webassembly would be possible.
